title: Gemini CLI MCP Server Setup in 2026 (10-Minute Guide)
summary: Gemini MCP server connections have operational constraints and hit predictable issues. Understand capacity expectations and how to handle common errors.
body_markdown:
## Run Gemini MCP tools and restrict access


Once a server shows CONNECTED, all it has proven is that it can start. It hasn't proven it can do anything, so the next step is to make Gemini CLI call one of its tools and approve the prompt it raises.


### Run your first Gemini MCP tool call


Ask for something that can only be answered by the server, such as "list the files in the allowed directory" for a filesystem server. Gemini CLI will stop and show a confirmation prompt naming the server and the tool.


Choose "Allow once" the first time. If you pick "always allow" now, you have granted that permission before seeing what the tool returns.


If the prompt never appears and the model answers from its own knowledge, the tool wasn't offered to it. Run` /mcp` again and check that the tool is listed under the server. That mismatch is a discovery problem, not a model problem.


In the screenshot below, a different product's agent builder shows an empty Tools panel and an "Add tool" menu. It makes the same point as` /mcp` : until a tool is listed there, the model has nothing to call.


### Stage 5: connect a remote HTTP or SSE server


Use` httpUrl` for a streamable HTTP server and` url` for an SSE server; putting a streamable endpoint under` url` is a common cause of a handshake that never completes.


Add` headers` for a static token, or let the CLI run OAuth when the server asks for it.


Few servers are remote.[MCPtrove](https://mcptrove.com/) puts **89% of public MCP servers on stdio** , 9% on streamable HTTP and 2% on SSE, so implementing stdio support covers almost all servers.


So most tutorials you copy from assume a local process, and their` command` and` args` block won't translate to a hosted endpoint.


With SSE at 2%, when you have a choice, you're unlikely to find a server that requires it.


### Stage 6: limit tools and set trust


When a name appears in both lists, **the exclusion wins** :` includeTools` is an allowlist and` excludeTools` is a denylist. Use the allowlist for any server that exposes write or delete operations.


**` trust: true` skips the approval prompt for that server entirely.** Keep it off for anything you didn't write, and for a server you did write, turn it on only after you have read what each tool does.
